liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deep Elem Blues** (3 reviews): Played electric, which is rare; Called a gem, with Jerry clearly enjoying himself [12][17][21]
- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (2 reviews): This version appears on the Postcards of the Hanging CD; Listening to Postcards of the Hanging's version alongside this audience tape is recommended [14][22]
- **C.C. Rider** (1 review): Brent tears the show open here after a slow start with a flubbed opener [12]
- **Althea** (1 review): Singled out along with Cassidy and Bertha as very good versions [17]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 other source): The space leading into Spanish Jam is included within that track [2]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): The noodling transition from Drums into this song sounded like Spanish bullfight music [13]
- **Around And Around** (1 review): Smoking version, but the recording has a cut at its end [20]

## The recordings

- **gd81-12-03.nak700-mow.ford.28901.sbeok.flac** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 171 min; rated 4.64/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: This version has plenty of bass and is much fuller than the other, extremely thin-sounding audience source; High-quality audience recording with an even mix; the band sounds tight [15][20]
- **gd1981-12-03.153801.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 170 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1981-12-03.158830.mtx.seamons.ht148.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard levels run a little hot at times, especially guitars and vocals; 40 seconds missing near Drums/Space [4]
- **gd81-12-03.nak300.munder.6143.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 159 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [10]. Said about its sound: Among the clearer 1981 audience tapes, clearer than that year's soundboards, though the bass is weak and needs boosting; Reviewer prefers this recording's sound to the other source [12][17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer drove from Minneapolis to Madison through a bad blizzard to attend [13]
- Attendee recalls a snowstorm and a hall only about half full [19]
- Coliseum was a cozy smaller arena with good floor sound and general-admission floor; heavy snowstorm on the drive home [21]
- Reviewer vaguely recalls Billy storming off during Drums, leaving Mickey alone, but is unsure whether it was this show [21]
- Reviewer prefers this source over the alternative circulating audience tape of the date [15]
- Reviewer ranks it above the 2/78 Madison show on Dick's Picks, with a rollicking feel throughout [19]
- This source is judged superior to the later shnid 28901 audience source [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd81-12-03.nak700-mow.ford.28901.sbeok.flac**: taped by Doug Mow; transferred by Alex Ford; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [1]. Also: Recorded with two Nak 700 shotguns into a Sony TC-D5M on Maxell XLIIS tape; Alex Ford seeded the FLAC16 transfer to bt.etree.org on 04/08/05 [1]
- **gd1981-12-03.153801.nak304.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes ; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 capsules > Sony D5M (TDK SA-C90) [2]. Also: Master recording by Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller; Mow/Ford Nak 700 and Kevin Tobin matrix supply a 6:53 patch [2]
- **gd1981-12-03.158830.mtx.seamons.ht148.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) December 3, 2022 [4]. Also: Matrix begins at 1:07 of Jack Straw; Doug Mow's audience recording patches the end of He's Gone jam through most of Drums [4]
- **gd81-12-03.nak300.munder.6143.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak 300's [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by John Rottet Grateful Dead: [1981-12-03 Dane County Coliseum, Madison, WI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1981-12-03-dane-county-coliseum-madison-wi-usa/) [27]
